perf.summary: Unconditional MemClear forces an O(length) zeroing write pass on every allocation, even when the caller immediately overwrites the whole buffer.
perf.currentCost: UnsafeUtility.MemClear(Ptr, byteCount) touches every byte of the allocation (length * sizeof(T) stores), evicting useful cache lines and adding a full memory-write pass that callers who fully initialize the array (e.g. copy-from, fill, compute-into) pay for nothing.
perf.proposedChange: Add an overload / parameter mirroring Unity's convention: `UnsafeArray(int length, Allocator allocator, NativeArrayOptions options)` and only call MemClear when `options == NativeArrayOptions.ClearMemory`. Keep the existing 2-arg ctor delegating with ClearMemory for source compatibility, or add an explicit `bool clear` named-constant-driven path. Hot callers then pass UninitializedMemory and skip the pass.
perf.rationale: Eliminates an entire length-proportional store pass and its cache pollution for the common 'allocate then fully write' pattern; this is the standard NativeArray/UnsafeList design for exactly this reason. Pure constant-factor on small arrays but asymptotically the dominant cost when the caller's own init is also O(length).
perf.risk: Semantics change ONLY for callers that rely on zero-initialization; the default path must remain clearing to preserve observable behavior. Document that UninitializedMemory yields garbage contents. No Burst/blittability impact (NativeArrayOptions is a plain enum).

perf.summary: `this = default;` zeroes the whole struct and is then immediately followed by writing all three fields, doubling writes to Length/Allocator/Ptr.
perf.currentCost: `this = default` issues a struct-wide zero store (Ptr=0, Length=0, Allocator=0) and the next three lines overwrite the same slots, so each field is written twice. The struct is tiny (8+4+4 bytes) so the win is small but the zeroing is redundant.
perf.proposedChange: Drop `this = default;` and assign every field directly: `Length = length; Allocator = allocator; Ptr = (T*)AllocatorManager.Allocate(...);`. All instance fields are definitely assigned, so the struct ctor is fully initialized without the default-zero step.
perf.rationale: Removes one redundant struct-wide store; each field is written exactly once. Fewer instructions on the allocation hot path.
perf.risk: None for behavior: every field is unconditionally assigned afterward, so removing the default-zero is observably identical. Only required because C# struct ctors must definitely-assign all fields — direct assignment already satisfies that.

perf.summary: `this = default;` in Dispose does a struct-wide zero store even when Ptr was already null.
perf.currentCost: On every Dispose, `this = default` writes the full struct. For a struct passed by value/copied this is dead work, and it forces nulling Length/Allocator that callers cannot observe after disposal.
perf.proposedChange: Set only `Ptr = null;` after Free (so a double-Dispose is still safe via the null check) instead of `this = default;`. Length/Allocator do not need clearing for correctness.
perf.rationale: Single pointer store instead of a full-struct zero; keeps the idempotent double-free guard (Ptr null check) intact with strictly less work.
perf.risk: Behavior differs only if external code reads Length/Allocator after Dispose and expects 0 — disposed-object field reads are already undefined by convention, so this is semantics-preserving for valid usage. Keep `Ptr = null` to preserve the existing double-Dispose safety.
